claims.text: High-temperature solutionizing above 1500°C followed by quenching produces a single-phase disordered BCC MoNbTaW alloy.
Aging solutionized MoNbTaW at 700–800°C for several hours can induce nanoscale B2 precipitates.
The aging treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale B2 precipitates within the disordered BCC matrix.
The nanoscale B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion from the B2 precipitates increases yield strength through precipitation hardening.
The precipitate-containing microstructure will still permit controlled plastic slip and thereby preserve ductility.
Controlled aging will improve yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to solutionized-and-quenched MoNbTaW.
Controlled aging will enhance work-hardening response relative to solutionized-and-quenched MoNbTaW.
The predicted strength improvement will occur while ductility remains within acceptable limits.
High-temperature solutionizing is required to homogenize the alloy before aging.
An inert atmosphere during aging is needed to prevent oxidation.
Overly aggressive aging can cause excessive precipitate volume fraction or precipitate coarsening.
Excessive precipitate volume fraction or coarsening can cause brittleness and reduced ductility.
Nonuniform precipitate distributions can prevent achievement of the proposed strength–plasticity balance.
